title: Historical Emergence of Psychology as a Science
summary: How psychology became an independent experimental discipline: Wilhelm Wundt's 1879 Leipzig laboratory, the five-stage evolution of psychology's subject matter, and Wundt's components of thought (representations, feelings, will).

notes.t: Before 1879, questions about the mind, the soul and behaviour belonged to philosophy and physiology rather than to a separate experimental discipline. Greek philosophers — Socrates, Plato and Aristotle — asked the questions that psychology now answers empirically, about the soul, knowledge, the mind–body relation and the origins of thought.
1879: Wilhelm Wundt and the First Experimental Laboratory

Wilhelm Wundt, a German physiologist and philosopher, is widely regarded as the father of experimental psychology. He established psychology's first experimental laboratory at the University of Leipzig, Germany, in 1879. This event is the conventional date for the birth of psychology as an independent experimental science. Wundt aimed to study conscious experience using controlled experiment and introspection.
1879 — Wilhelm Wundt opens the first experimental psychology laboratory at the University of Leipzig, Germany. Regarded as the birth of psychology as an independent experimental discipline.
Wundt and the Components of Thought

According to Wundt, the fundamental unit of the mind is thought, which he categorised into three components: representations, feelings and will. He introduced the concepts of voluntarism and Völker psychology.

Wundt's work played a key role in establishing psychology as a laboratory-based, experimental discipline. His emphasis on analysing the constituents or 'building blocks' of the mind laid the groundwork for the structuralist school developed by his student Edward B. Titchener.

notes.c: Five stages in the evolution of psychology's subject matter

notes.t: This five-stage framing is the standard academic account of how psychology's subject matter evolved. Psychology's subject matter kept expanding — each stage added rather than replaced the last.
Do not date Wundt's laboratory to anything but 1879. 'Behaviour and mental processes' is the modern definition — earlier single-focus answers (soul only, mind only, behaviour only) are incomplete.
